title: macOS Desktop App
content:
Botmux Desktop is the Mac app for botmux. It ships with its own runtime, so you don't need Node or a global botmux command. Double-click it to start the background service, browse the Dashboard, and read logs.

It's a good fit when:

You run botmux on a Mac and want a window with start / stop buttons instead of remembering commands.

You'd rather not deal with Node versions on your machine.

You want botmux to start in the background when you log in to your Mac.

For Linux servers or dev boxes, keep using the command-line install in Quick Start. The desktop app is macOS only.

How it relates to the CLI

Desktop app	CLI (curl / npm install)
Runtime	Bundled in the app, same version as the app	The botmux program you installed
Config, sessions, logs	All in ~/.botmux	All in ~/.botmux (the same one)
Bot processes	Started by the app's runtime	Started by botmux start

Both sides read and write the same ~/.botmux: bot config (bots.json), sessions, logs, and the background process records are shared. Moving from the CLI to the desktop app doesn't require reconfiguring your bots.

But only one side can manage the bots at a time. When the app opens it takes them over automatically; see What happens when the app opens.

Install

Open GitHub Releases and find the latest stable release.

Download Botmux-<version>-mac-universal.dmg (or the .zip with the same name) from the assets.
It's a Universal build: works on both Intel and Apple silicon (M-series) Macs.

The package is signed and notarized by Apple, so macOS won't block it when you open it.


Open the DMG and drag Botmux into the Applications folder.

Launch Botmux from Applications or Launchpad.

Only stable releases include the desktop package. Preview builds such as -canary or -beta are CLI only. The package is attached after the release is published, so it may not show up during the first few minutes.

Before you start: the AI CLIs you plan to use (such as claude or codex) still need to be installed and logged in from a terminal, and tmux is required by default. See Prerequisites. The app reads the PATH from your shell config (zsh / bash / fish profile and rc files), so any command your terminal can find, the app's bots can find too.

First run

You've used the CLI before: just open the app. It picks up the bots already in ~/.botmux, takes them over, and starts them.

You've never configured a bot: the bottom-left corner shows "Setup needed" and the dashboard can't load. Add your first bot first:

Run botmux setup once from a terminal. A Feishu QR scan creates the app for you. This step needs the CLI installed first; see steps 1 and 2 of Quick Start. Then go back to the app and click "Start".

Or write ~/.botmux/bots.json by hand following bots.json ("Open folder" in the app's top bar opens that directory).

Once the first bot exists and the service is running, you can add more bots with "Add bot" in the app's top bar.

Everyday use

The app has three areas:

Area	What it does
Left sidebar	Dashboard pages (Overview, Sessions, Groups, Schedules, Bot Profiles, etc.); at the bottom, the runtime status, "Start / Stop / Restart" buttons, and the "Launch app at login" switch
Top bar	Online daemons, items needing attention, configured bots; "Create session", "Add bot", "Docs", "Logs", "Open folder"; 中 / EN switch
Center	The embedded Dashboard, used exactly like in a browser; see Dashboard

Common tasks:

I want to…	Do this
Start / stop / restart all bots	The buttons in the bottom-left corner, or Start / Stop / Restart Botmux in the menu bar icon
Read logs	"Logs" in the top bar; pick a process in the drawer and copy with one click. "Open folder" opens ~/.botmux/logs
Run automatically after logging in	Turn on "Launch app at login". The app starts quietly in the background and brings the bots up
Close the window	The red close button only hides the window; bots keep running. Click the menu bar icon to reopen it

The menu bar icon's menu:

Show Console        Open the window
Start Botmux        Start
Stop Botmux         Stop
Restart Botmux      Restart
Open Logs           Open the logs folder
Open Botmux Home    Open ~/.botmux
Quit App            Quit the app

"Quit App" only quits the app itself; it does not stop the bots. To stop them too, click "Stop" before quitting.

What happens when the app opens

On launch, the app checks who is currently running the bots:

Current state	What the app does
Nothing running	Starts them with the bundled runtime
Already run by the app	Nothing; it just shows the status
Started by the CLI botmux start (or a version different from the app's)	Gracefully stops those processes first, then brings them back up with the bundled runtime

In the last case the bottom-left corner briefly shows a message saying it detected an external botmux runtime and is switching to the bundled one. This is a normal handover; your CLI install isn't being broken:

Nothing in ~/.botmux is deleted or changed.

Like a regular botmux restart, sessions in progress are restored after the restart.

Only botmux's own core processes are replaced; plugin services are left alone.

Also, while the app is open, if you run botmux restart / botmux start in a terminal, the app notices within a few seconds and takes the bots back. This keeps two versions from connecting to the same bots at once.

Switching back to the CLI

To manage the bots with the botmux command in your terminal again:

Click "Stop" in the app (optional, but saves one restart).

Turn off "Launch app at login" so the app doesn't take over again at your next login.

Choose "Quit App" from the menu bar icon (or press ⌘Q).

In a terminal, run botmux start (if you stopped first) or botmux restart (if you didn't).

As long as the app isn't open, the CLI keeps managing the bots. If you open the app again later, it takes over using the rules above.

If both autostarts are on (the app's "Launch app at login" and the CLI's botmux autostart enable), the CLI brings the bots up at login and then the app takes them over. It works, but costs an extra restart. Keep just one: if you use the app, run botmux autostart disable; if you use the CLI, turn off the app's switch.

Upgrading

Download the new DMG, drag the new Botmux into Applications to replace the old one, and open the app.

When the app sees running processes from a different version, it restarts them once with the new version. Desktop upgrades follow the app only: botmux update or re-running the curl install script upgrades the CLI, not the app.

FAQ

The app keeps showing "Needs attention" and the dashboard won't load?
Open "Logs" in the top bar first. Common causes: ~/.botmux/bots.json is malformed (the bottom-left corner tells you which entry is wrong), or the app is still taking over from the CLI; wait a few seconds.

Bots say they can't find claude / codex?
The app uses the PATH from your shell config. First make sure which claude works in a freshly opened terminal. If you installed the CLI or changed your shell config after the app was opened: quit the app ("Quit App" in the menu bar), open it again, then click "Restart" so the bots pick up the new PATH. Reopening the app alone isn't enough, because quitting the app doesn't stop the running bots.

The app quits right after opening?
Usually the app bundle is incomplete (for example, an interrupted copy). Download the DMG again and reinstall over it.

Bots still reply after I quit the app?
That's expected. Quitting the app doesn't stop the service; click "Stop" first.

Can I use the desktop app and the CLI together?
You can keep both installed, and they share the same config, but only one runs the bots at a time. While the app is open, the app manages them; after you quit it, the CLI can. CLI commands that only look and don't change anything (such as botmux status or botmux logs) work any time.

title: Feishu Doc Comment Watching (/watch-comment)
content:
Let the bot "live" in a Feishu/Lark cloud doc: ask a question or make a request in a doc comment, the AI reads the doc and does the work, then posts its answer straight back into that comment's thread. No need to leave the doc or switch to a group.

Good for:

Asking "does this section match the code?" while reading a design doc

Having the AI rewrite, extend, or review a passage in the doc

Letting the AI pre-read a doc before a meeting, so everyone can ask in comments during the meeting

Quickest start: @ the bot in a comment

No command needed. Open any Feishu doc the bot can access and @the bot in a comment with your question.

When the bot picks it up, it adds a "Typing" reaction to your comment and removes it once the answer is posted.

The answer is posted as the bot's identity in the original comment thread, and @s the person who asked.

The doc is automatically registered as a "reply only when @ the bot" watch, so later @bot comments in the same doc are handled too.

Each comment thread in the doc gets its own session, so conversations don't mix.

If the person mentioning the bot is not the bot owner, the bot still replies right away, but only after it manages to DM the owner a notice: who mentioned it, in which doc. If that notice can't be sent (or the bot has no owner configured), the bot doesn't reply and the auto-registration is undone. This is "notify, don't approve": the owner always knows, but replies don't wait for approval. To stop replying in a doc, the owner sends /watch-comment off <doc link>.

This zero-command path relies on Feishu pushing the comment event to the bot. If the first mention gets no response, check "One-time setup" below, or register explicitly with /watch-comment.

Bind to a topic: /watch-comment

To have comments share one AI session with a Feishu topic (for example, a topic already discussing this project), send this in that topic:

/watch-comment <Feishu doc link> [--dir <local project path>] [--all | --mentions-only | --owner-mentions]

After that:

If the topic has no AI session yet, one is created and the CLI starts right away;

The AI reads the doc first to build context, then waits for comments;

Matching comments in the doc are fed into this session, and answers go back to the original comment thread;

Status cards, terminal links, and other cards still go to this topic.

To answer with local code in mind, pass a project directory with --dir. Without it, the topic session's current working directory is used. If there is none, the AI answers from the doc alone, and the receipt reminds you that you can add one with /cd <project dir>.

Every form of /watch-comment (register, list, off) is bot-owner only. Everyone else can only trigger replies by @-ing the bot in the doc.

Commands

Command	What it does
/watch-comment <doc link> [--dir <path>] [mode]	Register a watch and bind it to the current topic session
/watch-comment list	Inside a session: docs watched by this session. Without a session: all doc watches of this bot
/watch-comment off <doc link>	Stop watching this doc
/watch-comment off or off all	Stop every watch in the current scope (this session / this bot)

Supports Feishu cloud docs (docx) and Wiki links.

Which comments trigger: three modes

Mode	Flag	Who triggers the AI	Good for
Only @ the bot (default)	--mentions-only	Comments that @ the bot	Most docs, the quietest
Reply when the owner is @-ed (stand-in)	--owner-mentions	Comments that @ the watch owner (whoever ran /watch-comment) or @ the bot	Letting the bot answer questions people @ you with
Every new comment	--all	Any new comment in the doc, no @ needed	Bot-dedicated docs

Notes:

The stand-in and every-comment modes find new comments by reading the comment list about every 5 seconds, so there can be a few seconds of delay. Comments that really @ the bot still arrive instantly, and the two paths never handle the same comment twice.

When switching to one of those two modes, the bot only handles comments posted afterwards. It won't dig up old comments and answer them again.

Auto-registration (the zero-command path) always uses "only @ the bot". To change the mode, run /watch-comment <link> --all (or another flag) again, or change it in the Dashboard. The Dashboard only offers "only @ the bot" and "every new comment"; the stand-in mode can only be set with the command.

Use at most one mode flag. Passing several is an error.

Set the default mode

The default mode for new watches is set per bot in Dashboard → Bot Config under "Doc subscription trigger (default)": "Only when a comment @s me" or "Every new comment".

The matching bots.json field is docSubscribeDefaultMode: "all" means every new comment; leave it out for only @ the bot.

Pin a project directory to a doc

To have a doc always work in a fixed project directory, set docRepoMap in bots.json. Keys are doc tokens, values are absolute local paths:

{
  "docRepoMap": {
    "<doc token>": "/home/me/my-repo"
  }
}

docRepoMap only applies to watches not bound to a topic (zero-command auto-registrations and watches registered in the Dashboard). A watch bound to a topic uses the topic session's working directory; to change it, use --dir or /cd in the topic.

Manage it in the Dashboard

The Dashboard sidebar has a "Doc watches" page where you can manage everything without commands:

See the list: every watched doc, its bot, working directory, and trigger mode;

See how it's running: last activity, last delivery, total deliveries, and "why the latest comment wasn't answered";

Change mode / stop: switch the trigger range right on the card ("only @ the bot" or "every new comment"), or click "Stop watching";

Register a new doc: paste a doc link (or token), pick a bot and a trigger range, optionally fill in a working directory, then click "Start watching". A new doc isn't bound to any topic; a session is created when the first matching comment arrives. For a doc already bound to a topic, this only updates the mode and working directory, and comments still go back to that topic;

Spot the origin: watches auto-created by someone else @-ing the bot are marked, so the owner can review them.

When comments fail to be handled, a "Document comment failures" panel appears at the top of the Dashboard overview and sessions pages. Expand it to see why, and jump to "Doc watches". In the doc itself, an @ the bot couldn't handle also gets an error reaction, so the person asking knows to retry.

What the AI sees

Each comment is handed to the AI together with:

the doc link;

for an inline comment (one made on selected text), the selected source text;

earlier discussion in the same comment thread.

When the question needs the full body, the AI is told to read the doc with an available Feishu doc tool first instead of guessing.

How answers get back to the doc

By default, the answer is posted as the bot in the original comment thread, with the first part @-ing the person who asked;

Long answers are split into several comments automatically;

A few comments (for example resolved ones, or docs whose settings block replies) can't take replies. The bot then creates a new whole-doc comment as the answer, so it always lands in the comment area;

If the bot itself has no access to the doc, it falls back to posting as the authorized user. To keep answers showing as the bot, share the doc with the bot;

Doc comments are a plain-text channel. Buttons, cards, and terminal links still go through the Feishu topic (doc sessions auto-created by the zero-command path post no cards and only reply in comments).

One-time setup (Feishu Open Platform)

/watch-comment needs no User Token. The bot reads comments and posts replies with its app identity. You only need to do two things for the app in the Feishu Open Platform console:

Permissions: enable docs:document.comment:read (read comments) and docs:document.comment:create (post comments/replies), plus wiki:wiki:readonly for Wiki docs, then publish a version;

Event subscriptions: add the drive.notice.comment_add_v1 (doc comment added) event, using long-connection delivery.

Once the bot has doc watches, its startup self-check verifies these permissions and DMs the admin if any are missing. Feishu can't auto-detect event subscriptions, so the self-check only reminds you to confirm it.

Lifecycle

/close on a topic session also removes the doc watches bound to it;

After a daemon restart, watches and the reading progress of the every-comment / stand-in modes are restored automatically, without re-answering old comments;

A doc binds to only one session at a time: running /watch-comment for the same doc in another topic moves it there, and the receipt tells you so;

One session can watch several docs at once.

Legacy command: /subscribe-lark-doc

/subscribe-lark-doc is the earlier approach, kept for those who need it. It requires a doc-scoped User Token, calls Feishu's per-file subscribe API, and binds the subscription to the current session. If the token is missing, the command gives you an authorization link; authorize and retry.

Command	What it does
/subscribe-lark-doc <doc link>	Subscribe to this doc with a User Token and bind it to the current session
/subscribe-lark-doc list	List docs subscribed by this session
/subscribe-lark-doc off	Unsubscribe all docs of this session

Prefer /watch-comment for new setups. You only need /subscribe-lark-doc when the zero-command path receives no events and you want to force Feishu's per-file subscription. Docs subscribed this way are unsubscribed through the Feishu API on /close.

title: Environment Variables and File Locations
content:
Most settings live in bots.json and the Dashboard, so you usually don't need environment variables. Only a few machine-wide switches (bind address, ports, external address, backend type, and so on) go in ~/.botmux/.env. This page lists those switches and where botmux keeps its key files, for backup and troubleshooting.

When to read this page: the Dashboard or web terminal won't open, you need to change a bind address or port, terminal links show the wrong address, you want the pty backend, or you're looking for config / logs / data.

This page covers botmux's own processes. To control which variables the CLI inside a session receives, use the Dashboard: "Settings → Session environment" (global) or "Bot settings → Advanced → Startup environment → Session environment" (per bot). See bots.json → Session environment.

How to change a setting

Edit ~/.botmux/.env, one KEY=value per line:

# ~/.botmux/.env
WEB_EXTERNAL_HOST=10.0.0.12
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PORT=7891

Restart to apply:

botmux restart

Put values in the file instead of only exporting them in a shell. A restart that a bot runs from inside a Feishu session reads only ~/.botmux/.env and does not inherit your shell. A value you only exported is lost on the next in-session restart.

Network and access addresses

These decide whether other people can open web terminal and Dashboard links.

Variable	Default	Purpose
WEB_HOST	0.0.0.0	Address the web terminal service listens on
WEB_EXTERNAL_HOST	Local LAN IP, auto-detected	Hostname / IP used in terminal links on cards. Set it when the machine has several NICs or you access it by domain (see Web Terminal)
BOTMUX_WEB_PROXY_BASE_PORT	8800	Each bot's terminal entry port = this value + bot index (bot 1 is 8800, bot 2 is 8801, …)
WEB_EXTERNAL_PORT	Unset, uses the local port	Set when a relay host exposes a different port than the local one. Also offset per bot: the real port is WEB_EXTERNAL_PORT + bot index
BOTMUX_WORKER_HTTP_HOST	0.0.0.0	Listen address of each session's terminal sub-service (the old name BOTMUX_WORKER_HOST still works)
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_HOST	0.0.0.0	Dashboard listen address
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PORT	7891	Dashboard port. If it's taken, botmux tries the next free port; the actual port is written to ~/.botmux/.dashboard-port
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_EXTERNAL_HOST	WEB_EXTERNAL_HOST, then a non-wildcard listen address, then the LAN IP	Hostname used when botmux commands print Dashboard links
BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL	Unset	Set it when you put the Dashboard behind your own nginx (or similar) on one domain, e.g. https://botmux.example.com. Dashboard and card terminal links then become <this URL>/… and <this URL>/s/<session ID>, so you expose a single entry point instead of one port per bot
BOTMUX_DEVBOX_AUTO_EXPORT	On	On a Merlin Devbox, automatically creates a private short link for the Dashboard. Skipped when central-platform remote access or BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL is configured. Set 0 or false to turn it off; on failure botmux falls back to the local address
BOTMUX_DAEMON_IPC_BASE_PORT	7950	Internal port used between bot background processes = this value + bot index, local-only. Rarely needs changing unless ports collide

Which address Dashboard links use: central platform (when remote access is on) > BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL > Devbox short link > local host:port. Terminal links follow the same order, minus the Devbox short link.

Dashboard access control

Variable	Default	Purpose
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_PUBLIC_READONLY	true	Allows read-only browsing of the Dashboard (sessions, schedules, …) without a token, so stale links still work; writes still need a token. Set false to disable. Note: once you change this switch on the Dashboard "Settings" page, the value in ~/.botmux/config.json wins and the environment variable no longer applies
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_TERMINAL_CONTROL_TTL_MS	300000 (5 minutes)	How long you can type after "taking over" a terminal in the Dashboard, between 10 seconds and 15 minutes. It returns to read-only on expiry, release, or disconnect
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_CONTROL_AUDIT_PATH	~/.botmux/audit/dashboard-control.ndjson	Audit log for terminal takeover and similar actions. Records only time, user, session, and action, never typed input

Open the Dashboard from Feishu without logging in (optional)

Off by default. When on, you can open the Dashboard straight from a Feishu H5 app without a token in the link; only users on the allow list get in.

Variable	Description
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_ENABLED	Set true to enable
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_APP_ID / _APP_SECRET	Credentials of the Feishu app used for login
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_ALLOWED_OPEN_IDS	Users allowed to sign in, comma-separated (open_ids under that app)
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_BRAND	feishu (default) or lark
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_ENTRY_PATH	Login entry path, default /auth/feishu
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_SESSION_TTL_MS	Login lifetime, default 30 minutes, range 1 minute to 24 hours
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_SECURE_COOKIE	Set true when TLS terminates at an upstream proxy but BOTMUX_PUBLIC_URL isn't an https:// URL
BOTMUX_DASHBOARD_FEISHU_H5_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS	Number of reverse proxies in front of the Dashboard (default 0, range 0–8), so rate limiting sees the real client IP

These variables (including the app secret) are used only by the Dashboard process. Bot background processes and session CLIs never receive them.

Sessions and behavior

Variable	Default	Purpose
BACKEND_TYPE	tmux	Session backend. tmux is always the default; if tmux is unavailable you get a card telling you so, and botmux does not silently switch to pty. Only an explicit pty selects the plain pty backend, and pty sessions don't survive a botmux restart (see tmux backend)
BOTMUX_FORWARD_FOLLOWUP_WAIT_MS	1500	After a new topic is posted in a topic group, how long to wait for the same person's immediate follow-up so both go to the CLI together. 0 disables, max 10000
BOTMUX_SENDER_RESOLVE_TIMEOUT_MS	800	Per-step timeout (ms) for looking up the sender's display name. Try 3000 on slow networks (at most 6 seconds if both steps time out). Owner identity checks keep their own 3-second budget
BOTMUX_ASK_TIMEOUT_MS	86400000 (24 hours)	How long a CLI question turned into a Feishu card waits for an answer. After a timeout the question falls back to the terminal and can no longer be answered from Feishu, so the default is long on purpose. Shortening it is not recommended
BOTMUX_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS	600000 (10 minutes)	How long a tool-permission card waits. On timeout the request is denied and the session keeps going. Clamped to 1 second–14 minutes
STUCK_DETECTOR_ENABLED	On	When an input hasn't finished a turn for a while, checks whether the CLI is stuck on a Codex hook-review screen and warns you if so. Set false to disable
STUCK_DETECTOR_TIMEOUT_MS	45000	How long (ms) after an input the check above runs
BOTMUX_SCHEDULE_TIMEZONE	Unset: the timezone chosen on the page, else the host timezone	Timezone for scheduled tasks, e.g. Asia/Shanghai. Takes priority over the timezone chosen on the Global Settings page; invalid names are ignored
BOTMUX_RECOVERY_FORK_BATCH	5	When botmux restarts and recovers sessions, how many it relaunches per batch, so they don't all start at once and swamp the machine. Minimum 1
BOTMUX_RECOVERY_FORK_DELAY_MS	250	Pause (ms) between recovery batches. Minimum 0
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_ENABLED	Off	Set true to name new worktree branches with AI. See "Name worktrees with AI" below
BOTMUX_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_SCOPES	Unset	Set 1 to request Feishu scopes not yet in botmux's scope list (syntax check only). A stopgap when Feishu ships a new scope before a botmux release
BOTMUX_CODEX_NODE_REPL_PATH	Unset	Absolute path to an installed Codex node_repl executable, for opt-in browser features when no MCP runtime is configured

BOTMUX_ASK_TIMEOUT_MS and BOTMUX_PERMISSION_TIMEOUT_MS are read by the CLI inside the session, which inherits them from ~/.botmux/.env by default. Because they start with BOTMUX, they are botmux-reserved and can't be set per bot in the session environment. When a bot uses strict process environment, they don't reach the session and the defaults apply.

Name worktrees with AI (optional)

Off by default. When botmux auto-names a new worktree branch (e.g. /repo wt), it uses a local naming rule. When on, it calls an OpenAI-compatible API you configure instead, and sends the topic title / first message to that API. When off, incomplete, or the request fails, the local rule is used.

Variable	Default	Purpose
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_ENABLED	Off	Set true to enable
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_BASE_URL	Unset	API base URL, required, e.g. https://api.example.com/v1. botmux appends /chat/completions
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_API_KEY	Unset	API key, required
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_MODEL	Unset	Model name, required
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_TIMEOUT_MS	5000	Request timeout (ms)
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_EXTRA_HEADERS	Unset	Extra request headers as a JSON string, e.g. {"X-Team":"dev"}. Ignored if not valid JSON
BOTMUX_WORKTREE_SLUG_AI_EXTRA_BODY	Unset	Extra request body fields as a JSON string. Ignored if not valid JSON

Host overload alert

Turn the overload alert on and pick the notification bot on the Dashboard "Global Settings" page (see Global Settings). The variables below fine-tune the thresholds; the enter thresholds take priority over the values on the page.

Variable	Default	Purpose
BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ALERT	Unset	Set 0 to turn the overload alert off completely, whatever the page says
BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ENTER_LOAD_RATIO	1.5	Overloaded when the 15-minute load average exceeds CPU count × this value
BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_EXIT_LOAD_RATIO	1.0	Recovered only once load drops to CPU count × this value or below
BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ENTER_MEM_FRAC	0.92	Overloaded when the used-memory fraction (0–1) reaches this value
BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_EXIT_MEM_FRAC	0.85	Recovered only once the used-memory fraction drops to this value or below
BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_MIN_REALERT_MS	900000 (15 minutes)	Minimum gap between two "entered overload" alerts

Exit thresholds must be lower than enter thresholds. If one isn't, botmux sets it to 95% of the enter threshold and logs a warning.

Paths, logs, and GitHub

Variable	Default	Purpose
BOTS_CONFIG	Unset, uses ~/.botmux/bots.json	Use a different bots.json file
SESSION_DATA_DIR	~/.botmux/data	Where sessions, queues, and other data are stored. On startup botmux records the actual location in ~/.botmux/.data-dir so command-line tools follow it
BOTMUX_WORKFLOW_RUNS_DIR	~/.botmux/workflow-runs	Workflow run records
DEBUG	Unset	Set 1 to enable debug logs
GITHUB_TOKEN	Unset	Token botmux uses for its own GitHub requests (Dashboard changelog, update checks, restart report) to avoid rate limits
GH_TOKEN	Unset	Same, used only when GITHUB_TOKEN is unset

GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN are used only for botmux's own GitHub requests and are not passed to session CLIs by default. If a bot's sessions need one, add it to that bot's session environment.

Advanced / special environments

Variable	Default	Purpose
BOTMUX_COMPANION_SECRET_FILE	Unset	Secret-file path for the Local Companion API, usually set by botmux start/restart --companion-secret-file. Must be an absolute path to a non-empty regular file owned by the current user, mode 0600, not a symlink. Never passed to session CLIs and never falls back to .dashboard-secret
BOTMUX_COMPANION_BOT_APP_ID	Unset	The single test bot bound to the Companion API, usually set by --companion-bot. Callers can't pick another bot
BOTMUX_LOOPBACK_PEERS	Empty	Only for unusual kernels that report same-machine connections as a LAN IP, causing Dashboard or internal calls to be rejected. Extra allowed source addresses, comma-separated IPs / CIDRs, e.g. 10.0.0.5,192.168.0.0/16

Notes on BOTMUX_LOOPBACK_PEERS:

Empty by default: only 127.0.0.1 and ::1 are accepted, same as older versions.

It relaxes only the "request must come from this machine" check. Signature, timestamp, and replay checks still apply, so a badly signed request is still rejected.

Entries that are too broad (/0–/7) or malformed are ignored with a startup warning.

Prefer a single address (/32) or the smallest real subnet. Write IPv4 addresses in IPv4 form: 10.0.0.0/8 covers both plain IPv4 and the dual-stack ::ffff:10.x form.

File locations

Path	What it is
~/.botmux/bots.json	Bot configuration
~/.botmux/.env	The environment variables on this page
~/.botmux/config.json	Global settings saved from the Dashboard "Settings" page; see Global Settings
~/.botmux/data/	Session data, message queues, etc. (change with SESSION_DATA_DIR)
~/.botmux/logs/	Background process logs; also viewable with botmux logs
~/.botmux/bin/botmux	Entry script for the global botmux command (written automatically)
~/.botmux/lark-scopes.json	Full list of recommended Feishu scopes (written during setup; copy it into the open platform's bulk import)
~/.botmux/.dashboard-port	The port the Dashboard actually listens on
~/.botmux/.dashboard-secret	Dashboard signing secret (mode 0600, keep it private)
~/.botmux/audit/	Dashboard terminal-takeover audit log

For backups, keep at least bots.json, .env, config.json, and data/.

title: FAQ / Troubleshooting
content:
Collected from the README and frequent questions in the community group, and updated over time. For more pitfalls, see Common Pitfalls.

This page is grouped by topic:

You want to fix	Go to
The bot doesn't reply, others can't use it, results never arrive	The bot doesn't reply
Grants, mention policy, adding the bot to groups	Permissions and mentions
Restarts, suspending, interrupting, working directories, terminal won't load on a phone	Sessions
Login errors, upgrades, fonts, wrappers	Install and environment

The bot doesn't reply

Match your symptom first — each one has a different cause:

Symptom	Likely cause	Jump
No reaction at all (not even an emoji)	Event subscription, release, or long connection not working	A. No messages at all
Only I (the owner) can trigger it; others get an auth card or no reply	Others have no talk permission	B. Others can't use it
It only replies when @-mentioned and you want it to reply without @	The group's mention policy	B. Others can't use it
The card says "working" and the terminal has output, but nothing reaches Lark	The model didn't call botmux send	C. Terminal has output but nothing reached Lark
The session won't start, and the first message errors with zsh: parse error	The login shell's startup file switches shells	Session does not start

A. No messages at all

Check in order (PersonalAgent comes configured; normally you don't need to touch this):

Event subscription: Open Platform → Events & Callbacks — subscribe to im.message.receive_v1 and card.action.trigger, choose "Long connection (WebSocket)", and make sure the daemon is running.

Bot capability: Open Platform → App Features → Bot is enabled.

Release: the app must have a published version ("visible only to me" is approved automatically). After changing permissions or events you must publish again for them to take effect.

Long connection taken: make sure no other program is using the same app's long connection.

Once all of that checks out, run botmux restart from a clean shell.

To have an agent investigate, see "General troubleshooting approach" in Common Pitfalls: use botmux logs to find the launch command and reproduce it locally, then check the real error in the web terminal.

B. Others can't use it

botmux has two permission layers:

Talk permission: who can talk to it.

Operate permission: who can run management commands such as /cd, /restart, /close, and tap card buttons.

By default only people in allowedUsers can talk to it. Anyone else who @-mentions it is blocked, and the owner gets a grant request card. Adding the bot to a group does not grant anyone access.

You want to	Do this
Let the whole group use it	Send @bot /grant in the group, or open the group's manage dialog in Dashboard Group Management and click Whole-chat grant
Let one person try it	@bot /grant @someone — 3 messages / 1 hour by default, adjustable on the card
Grant several people at once	Multi-select in the Dashboard group member list for a batch grant (up to 50 people)
Have it reply without an @	Change the mention policy with /mention-mode — see Why must I mention the bot in groups?
Run duty Q&A with one group per ticket	Use On-Call Mode
Block someone	Add them to the blocklist blockedUsers in Dashboard Bot Config; they're blocked in groups and DMs, with no more request cards

Full rules: Permissions & Access.

C. Terminal has output but nothing reached Lark

Output printed in the terminal is not the same as a message sent to Lark. For CLIs that send explicitly (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity, CoCo, and others), the model must run botmux send for the group to see anything:

Every send needs one of --mention-back, --mention, or --no-mention; otherwise it errors and sends nothing.

If it only uses echo / print, or forgets botmux send, nothing goes out.

Pass multi-line content with a heredoc; don't write "line one\nline two".

Two cases where the model doesn't need to send by itself:

codex-app (the Codex App protocol): botmux forwards the final reply automatically. Don't call botmux send for normal replies or they'll be posted twice; use it only for mid-turn progress, attachments, or @-mentioning another bot.

Zero prompt injection mode (promptInjection: "none"): botmux picks the final answer from the CLI's transcript and posts it to Lark. See bots.json.

Permissions and mentions

How are permissions divided? Who can operate the bot?

Source	Grants	Notes
allowedUsers	Operate + talk	The owner and admins. Can run management commands, tap buttons, and change /card /cot /mention-mode
allowedChatGroups (@bot /grant)	Talk	Whole group, no quota, no expiry
On-call groups	Talk	Whole group, and the group is bound to a working directory
chatGrants / globalGrants (/grant @someone)	Talk	Per person, 3 messages / 1 hour by default
blockedUsers	Deny everything	Takes priority over every rule above

Quotas, expiry, and request cards are covered in Permissions & Access.

How do I let a whole group use it?

Send @bot /grant (same as /grant all) in the group:

The group is added to allowedChatGroups, and everyone in it can talk right away — no message limit, no expiry.

New members get access automatically; people who leave lose it.

In a topic group it applies to the whole group, covering every topic.

Revoke with @bot /revoke.

The group manage dialog in Dashboard Group Management also has a Whole-chat grant button. It grants talk only; operate permission stays with allowedUsers.

How do I give someone a few trial messages?

Send @bot /grant @someone. The bot replies with a grant card that defaults to 3 messages / 1 hour per person.

To set the count directly: @bot /grant @someone 20.

Duration options are 1 hour, 8 hours, 1 day, 7 days, and permanent; leave the quota empty for unlimited.

What's the difference between on-call and /grant?

Both grant talk only, and neither has a quota. The difference is the working directory:

/oncall bind <dir> binds the group to a directory, so new topics skip repo selection and start right away. Good for duty Q&A.

/grant only opens up talking and binds no directory. Good when group members ask questions in topics whose repo is already chosen.

Why must I mention the bot in groups?

The default policy is always: in regular groups the bot replies only when explicitly @-mentioned, so bots don't talk over each other in groups with several bots or people. Send /mention-mode in the group to change it:

Mode	Effect
always (default)	@ required
topic	No @ needed for replies inside its own topics
never	No @ needed anywhere in the group
ambient	No @ needed, but it stays quiet when someone else is named

Changing it requires operate permission and works in regular groups only.

A "1 person + 1 bot" group needs no @ by default; you can turn that exception off with soloGroupMentionBypass.

A few more exceptions exist (message listeners, no-@ commands, and so on). See Mention Policy for the full list.

How do multiple bots work together?

It works out of the box — add the bots to the same group:

Just you and one bot: talk to it directly, no @ needed.

A group with several bots or people: @ the bot you want to hand the work to.

Bot-to-bot relays (say, one writes and another reviews): the bots @ each other; you only hand the work to the first one.

See Multi-bot Collaboration.

Can I stop people from adding the bot to groups?

Not from botmux. "Who can add the bot to a group" is controlled by the Lark platform (app availability, who can add bots to groups). What you can do on the bot side:

Don't auto-start when added: turn off Auto-start when added to a new chat (autoStartOnGroupJoin) under Dashboard Bot Config → Proactive Start. Even when it's on, the group must contain at least one person from allowedUsers.

Stay restricted: being added is not a grant. People without access are blocked when they @ it, and the owner gets a request card.

Don't pull the owner into new groups: by default, when the bot is added to a new group it also adds the owner (autoInviteOwnerOnGroupAdd). If an alert or on-call platform creates groups in bulk and the owner shouldn't be disturbed, turn off Add the owner to chats the bot joins under Bot Config → Proactive Start, send /botconfig set autoInviteOwnerOnGroupAdd off, or edit bots.json.

Can a bot added to a new group read earlier chat history?

Yes. Tell it "look at the chat history", or quote a specific message. The Lark app needs its full permission set (including reading group messages).

A regular group is too noisy — can I switch it to a topic group?

Yes, but the group owner or a group admin has to do it: Group Settings → Group Management → Message format → "Topic messages". The bot can't change group settings for you.

Sessions

Does restarting the daemon lose context?

Not with the default tmux backend. The CLI keeps running inside tmux, and after botmux restart the next message reattaches to the same process.

Without tmux installed, botmux does not quietly fall back to pty; it shows a card asking you to install tmux first.

pty is used only when you explicitly set BACKEND_TYPE=pty (or backendType: "pty" for one bot). pty sessions don't survive a daemon restart and have to be relaunched.

What happens to work in progress when the CLI restarts mid-way?

When the CLI exits unexpectedly (a crash, the tmux server going away, and so on), botmux relaunches it with the previous context and reads the transcript the old process left behind to see whether work was cut off:

the previous turn hadn't finished, such as a review half-way through;

background tasks died with the old process, such as Claude Code background commands, Monitors, or background agents.

If so, the resumed CLI first gets a short note (it was just restarted, which background tasks were interrupted, check and continue), and one notice appears in the topic. Nothing is posted when nothing was interrupted.

The same check runs on a cold resume after a suspend or a daemon restart; the note is placed in front of the next message to the CLI. CLIs that take the first message as a launch argument, such as Pi, only get the topic notice.

Only the transcript is read, never the screen. This covers Claude Code, plus CLIs with structured transcripts such as Pi and Codex (for those, only whether the turn finished).

Messages not yet handed to the CLI aren't lost:

A first message passed as a launch argument, where the CLI exited before starting on it, is typed in again after the restart.

Messages still queued when the daemon restarts are delivered by the session's next worker.

Messages older than 24 hours aren't re-delivered; the topic says they weren't delivered instead. The same happens when another restart interrupts re-delivery and delivery can't be confirmed.

A message the CLI had already received and started on is not typed in again; the note above reminds it to continue. It is re-sent only when the restart has to open a new session without the old context.

Does a session use memory forever if I don't close it?

No. Each bot has two automatic limits. A reclaimed session is "suspended": the CLI process exits and frees memory, but the topic stays, and the next message restores the context from disk (usually within a few seconds).

Rule	Default	Where to change it
Max resident sessions: beyond this, the least recently used session is suspended	30	Dashboard Bot Config → Resident session limit, or maxLiveWorkers in bots.json
Idle auto-suspend: suspend after N minutes of continuous idle	Off	Idle auto-suspend (minutes) in the same place, or idleSuspendMinutes in bots.json

A session that is producing an answer is never interrupted.

A session whose main turn has ended while background tasks keep running (the card shows "⏳ Main turn ended · background tasks running") isn't suspended either — suspending would kill those tasks, and they can't be brought back.

Adopted external terminals and sessions that can't be resumed are exempt.

To clean up by hand:

You want to	Command
Preview, then bulk-suspend sessions idle for 7 days	botmux maintenance suspend-idle --older-than 7d --dry-run, then replace --dry-run with --yes
Close one session	Send /close in the topic, or botmux delete <id>
Close all sessions	botmux delete all, or batch-close in the Dashboard
Clean up sessions whose process already exited	botmux delete stopped

More commands: CLI Commands.

Can I follow up or interrupt a running session?

By default it doesn't interrupt. New messages queue up and are entered in order after the current turn ends.

To stop and change course right away:

Tap ⏹ Stop on the card, or send /stop in the topic. It interrupts only the current turn; the session and its context stay.

When the card shows the terminal screenshot, you can also tap the Esc or ^C keys; in the web terminal you can press keys directly.

Then send your new request.

Wrong working directory or repository?

workingDir searches for git repos downward from that directory (up to 3 levels), never upward. Point it at a folder with many repos (such as ~/projects) to list them all; point it at one repo to list only that repo (and its worktrees).

Switch directories temporarily: /cd <path>.

Skip the repo picker and go straight into one repo: set defaultWorkingDir (see side effects in Common Pitfalls).

Don't set workingDir to ~ — there are too many folders to scan.

/repo numbers can change; use /repo <project-name> to pick a repo.

Session does not start

Symptom: the session never starts, or the first message errors with zsh: parse error near '\n'.

Usually your login shell ($SHELL, often bash) has a "switch to another shell" line in its startup file. The classic one is in ~/.bashrc:

if [ -t 1 ]; then exec zsh; fi   # common when chsh doesn't take effect

botmux starts the session inside tmux with <$SHELL> -i -c '…start the CLI'. -i loads that startup file, exec zsh replaces the shell, and the command that starts the CLI never runs — so the first message lands in an empty shell. botmux detects this and posts a diagnostic card instead of typing the message into the empty shell.

Pick one fix:

Set launchShell (recommended): start this bot directly with the target shell, skipping the startup file that switches shells.
In Lark, send /botconfig set launchShell zsh;

or fill it in under Dashboard Bot Config → Launch shell;

or add "launchShell": "zsh" to bots.json.

PATH, nvm, and the like must live in the chosen shell's own startup file (such as .zshrc; for fish, ~/.config/fish/config.fish).

Fix the startup file: only switch when you open a terminal by hand: [ -z "$BASH_EXECUTION_STRING" ] && [ -t 1 ] && exec zsh (put PATH, nvm, etc. before this line).

Then run botmux restart and send another message. This only affects backends that start through a shell (tmux / zellij / zmx); the pty backend starts the CLI directly and isn't affected.

The Workbench or terminal won't load on my phone?

If it works on your computer but on your phone the Workbench is blank or the terminal never shows up, open <your Dashboard address>/workbench-doctor in the phone's browser.

This self-check page needs no sign-in. It checks the service version, sign-in state (cookies), the terminal link and the live connections on its own.

When it finishes, send a screenshot to the bot or a maintainer. It shows whether the cause is the network, the sign-in state or a stale cache.

The page never shows any token or secret, so the screenshot is safe to share.

For what each check means, see Agent Workbench · Phone won't load it? Use the self-check page.

Install and environment

How do I upgrade?

The safest way is to re-run the install command, no matter how you installed originally (npm / pnpm global installs included):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepcoldy/botmux/master/install.sh | sh

It replaces ~/.botmux/bin/botmux in place. The download is test-run on your machine first; if it can't run, the installer errors out and keeps your current version.

You can run it again safely: it won't add PATH twice, and it doesn't need Node.

Afterwards, open a new terminal and run botmux restart. The installer puts ~/.botmux/bin at the front of PATH, and only a new terminal is guaranteed to pick up the new version.

The botmux command inside sessions always matches the daemon version; no separate upgrade needed.

On v3.18.0 or later you can also use the built-in command:

You want to	Command
Upgrade to the latest stable release	botmux update (botmux upgrade is the same)
Switch to a preview channel	botmux update canary (beta, rc, next also work)
Install a specific version	botmux update 3.28.0

Install a specific version with curl (same for rollback or pinning; the tag needs the v):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/deepcoldy/botmux/master/install.sh | BOTMUX_VERSION=v3.18.8 sh

⚠️ BOTMUX_VERSION must come right before the sh on the right of the pipe. If you write BOTMUX_VERSION=… curl … | sh, only curl sees the variable, sh doesn't, and you silently get the latest version.

Why can releases older than v3.18.0 only upgrade via curl?

From v3.18.0 the npm package switched from "Node + source" to platform binaries, and node-pty left the dependencies. Old releases' botmux upgrade handed the job to npm: crossing this version, npm deletes node-pty from the old directory, but the old daemon still loads it on restart, fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and none of the bots come back (the output may already say "restarting to apply the update"). curl drops in the new binary without relying on the old directory, so it's the one safe way across this version. If you're not sure how you installed, just use curl.

How do I fix Please run /login · API Error: 403?

First work out which side wants a login:

Lark authorization rejected (calling Lark APIs as the user failed): send /login in the topic, open the authorization link, then copy the address the browser lands on (http://127.0.0.1:9768/callback?... — it's normal that the page doesn't load) back into the topic.

The model gateway returns 403: unrelated to Lark; usually an environment variable or gateway token problem. A common cause is bash users putting variables in .bash_profile, which bash -i doesn't read (see Common Pitfalls).

claude keeps asking for /login on macOS

claude stores its login token in two places, and the two drifting apart is the main reason for Please run /login on macOS:

Where	Who uses it
Keychain item Claude Code-credentials	claude running in the GUI, and botmux's default (non-isolated) setup
File ~/.claude/.credentials.json	Running /login over SSH can only write here

As long as the keychain item exists, claude reads only the keychain, never the file. So "/login over SSH succeeded (it only wrote the file), but the GUI and the bot still use the old keychain token". On top of that, claude rotates the token on refresh, so whichever side refreshes first invalidates the other, and everyone gets logged out.

Stick to the file as the only source:

Don't use claude code in the GUI; it writes the token to the keychain.

Always update the token by running /login over SSH.

If an old keychain item already exists, delete it.

botmux history returns 400, or the Lark gateway returns 411?

400: usually the Lark app is missing a permission (such as im:message.group_msg). Enable the full permission list.

411: older versions sent GET requests with an empty body, which the Lark gateway rejects. Upgrade to a newer version.

Does it support Lark (international, larksuite.com)?

Yes. Both Feishu (feishu.cn) and Lark (larksuite.com) work:

When you scan to create an app, China vs. international is detected automatically; when you paste the AppID / Secret by hand, you choose once.

Each bot connects to the domain of its own edition. One machine can run Feishu and Lark bots side by side, with separate login credentials.

Can I launch the CLI through ccr, a custom gateway, or a wrapper?

Yes. Write a wrapper script that passes its arguments ("$@") straight through, then set cliPathOverride to that script's path when editing the bot in botmux setup.

Chinese characters or emoji show up as boxes in screenshots?

Fonts are missing. On Debian / Ubuntu the daemon tries to install fonts-noto-cjk and fonts-noto-color-emoji automatically (needs root or passwordless sudo). On other Linux distributions, install Noto CJK and Noto Color Emoji by hand, then restart the daemon.

A bot with cliId: "gemini" no longer starts?

Gemini CLI has been retired and the gemini adapter removed. That bot refuses to start with a hint to switch to Antigravity; other bots keep running. To migrate:

Install agy and sign in with a Google account (or set modelProvider: "gemini" in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json and provide GEMINI_API_KEY).

Change cliId to "antigravity" (in bots.json or with botmux setup).

Run botmux restart.

The old cliPathOverride / wrapperCli (such as ttadk gemini), Gemini model names, and GEMINI_CLI_HOME don't carry over. See CLI Adapters.

Messages sent while CoCo is busy get lost?

Upgrade to CoCo 0.120.32 or later. Messages sent while it's busy go into CoCo's own queue, which relies on that version's behavior.

Does it work on Windows?

Native Windows isn't supported: the daemon only runs on Unix-like systems, and there's no Windows build (neither curl nor npm can install one). Install inside WSL2 and follow the Linux steps there.

description: Collected from the README and frequent questions in the community group, and updated over time. For more pitfalls, see Common Pitfalls. This page is grouped by topic:

title: Feedback Storage & Migration
content:
Supabase

The optional Supabase backend uses @supabase/supabase-js and installation-bound
transactional RPCs. SQLite and PostgreSQL feedback sources can migrate directly
to an independently bootstrapped Supabase schema. Sessions and schedules remain
outside this migration.

Configure a candidate with backend: "supabase" and
supabase: { url, keyRef, schema, requestTimeoutMs }. Use an HTTPS project URL,
a private server secret reference such as env:SUPABASE_KEY, and a dedicated
schema. Configuring a candidate does not change active storage.

Generate SQL with botmux feedback storage supabase-schema; an administrator
must review and install it in the target project and expose that dedicated schema
through its Data API. The command only prints SQL and does not execute it.
Then test the saved connection with botmux feedback storage test.

After separate maintenance authorization, run from an independent host process:
botmux feedback storage migrate --to supabase --yes --request-id ORIGINAL_REQUEST_ID.
Use status and the original resume MIGRATION_ID after interruption. Unknown
mutations are reconciled from their original markers, never blindly replayed.
The source, snapshots, IDs, revision order and event-stream positions are retained.
After target writes begin, switching directly back to the stale source is unsafe.

botmux keeps "feedback data" in a database: user ratings of final answers, the outcome of each turn, the delivery queue for feedback webhooks, and so on. This is what the Dashboard "Feedback analytics" page shows.

SQLite by default: a local file, botmux-feedback.sqlite, in the botmux data directory (~/.botmux/data/ by default). Nothing to install, and most people never need anything else.

PostgreSQL if you want it: switch when you need central storage, backups, or to plug the data into your own analytics.

You switch storage with the botmux feedback storage command or with the "Feedback storage" panel on the Dashboard "Feedback analytics" page. Both can do the same things.

Which should I pick?

My situation	What to do
Fresh install, no special needs	Press Enter when the first botmux start asks about storage to keep SQLite
Fresh install, want PostgreSQL right away	Type postgresql at the first start, then give the config file path (see Step 1)
On SQLite, no feedback data yet	Empty database: enable directly
On SQLite, with history to keep	Migrate (needs a short downtime)
On PostgreSQL, want SQLite back or a different database	Not supported yet, see the FAQ

If the first start does not run in an interactive terminal (for example from a script), botmux uses SQLite without asking.

Three things to know before migrating

Service pauses during migration: once the "maintenance window" starts, new topics, new turns, and botmux send are refused, and restarted daemons wait, until the migration completes or is cancelled. Pick a quiet time.

No automatic fallback: after switching to PostgreSQL, botmux will not switch back to SQLite on its own if the database fails. The old SQLite file is kept but marked "retired" and no longer written.

Passwords never go on the command line or in the config file: only "secret references" are allowed, see How to supply the password.

Switch from the command line

Step 1: Prepare a config file

Create a JSON file, for example pg.json:

{
  "backend": "postgresql",
  "postgres": {
    "host": "db.example.com",
    "port": 5432,
    "database": "botmux",
    "user": "botmux",
    "schema": "botmux_feedback",
    "passwordRef": "env:BOTMUX_FEEDBACK_PG_PASSWORD",
    "tls": { "mode": "verify-full" },
    "connectTimeoutMs": 5000
  }
}

Field	Meaning
host / port / database / user	Connection details, all required
schema	A schema just for botmux. Pick a name that does not exist yet in the database; botmux creates it. Lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit
passwordRef	A reference to the password, not the password itself (see below)
tls.mode	verify-full: verify the server certificate (recommended); disable: no encryption
tls.caRef	Optional reference to a custom CA certificate, same format as passwordRef
connectTimeoutMs	Connection timeout, 100–60000 ms

Extra fields (such as a password key) are not allowed and the file will be rejected.

Step 2: Save it as the candidate and test it

botmux feedback storage configure --config-file ./pg.json
botmux feedback storage test
botmux feedback storage status

configure only saves it as the "candidate" config. It does not switch and does not touch any data.

test connects to the database and checks that the account has the CREATE privilege on it (botmux needs it to create its own schema and tables).

status shows the active storage (active), the candidate (candidate), and past migration jobs. Running botmux feedback storage with no subcommand also shows status.

All commands print JSON. On error they print {"error":"feedback_..."} and exit with code 1.

Step 3: Migrate

botmux feedback storage migrate --to postgresql --yes

--yes confirms that you accept the maintenance window; without it the command is refused. The command runs until it finishes and prints something like:

{"migrationId":"5dd49f52-...","phase":"complete","blockers":[]}

phase: complete means success (exit code 0), and feedback data now goes to PostgreSQL. Along the way it passes through these phases:

Phase	What happens
preflight	Connect to the target and prepare the tables
draining	Enter the maintenance window and wait for running turns to finish (about 45 seconds max)
snapshot	Take a read-only snapshot of SQLite
importing	Import the snapshot into PostgreSQL (the target must be empty)
verifying	Compare row counts and contents table by table
retiring / activating	Retire SQLite and switch to PostgreSQL
complete	Done, the maintenance window ends

If phase is blocked, the migration is stuck. See the next section.

Stuck: resume or cancel

When blocked, blockers tells you why. The maintenance window does not end on its own after a block, so new turns stay blocked until you pick one:

# After fixing the problem, continue the same job (safe to repeat)
botmux feedback storage resume <migrationId>

# Give up and restore the original SQLite
botmux feedback storage cancel <migrationId> --yes \
  --reason "Target lacks permissions, retry later" \
  --evidence "ticket:1234"

cancel needs --yes, --reason (why you cancel), and --evidence (what you checked, such as a ticket number). They are kept in an audit record.

Cancelling only restores SQLite. Data already written to PostgreSQL is not deleted.

Once SQLite has been marked retired (after the retiring phase finishes), you cannot cancel. Use resume to finish.

Common blockers:

Reason	What to do
feedback_maintenance_not_ready	Not ready within 45 seconds: turns are still running, a botmux send is in progress or has an unknown outcome, or a daemon did not respond. Wait for turns to finish; acknowledge unknown sends via Delivery recovery items, then resume
feedback_outbox_unsettled	There are webhook deliveries with unknown outcomes. See Delivery recovery items, then resume
feedback_storage_target_not_empty / feedback_migration_target_not_empty	The target schema already exists and was not created by botmux, or it already holds feedback data. Use a schema name that does not exist yet
feedback_storage_secret_missing	The password reference cannot be read (env var not set or file missing)
feedback_migration_database_or_io_error	A database or disk error, most often the database is unreachable or permissions are missing. Run test to narrow it down, fix it, then resume

No existing data: enable directly

If SQLite has no feedback data yet, you can skip the migration:

botmux feedback storage configure --config-file ./pg.json
botmux feedback storage enable-empty --yes

If SQLite holds even one row, enable-empty refuses (feedback_storage_migration_required). Use migrate instead.

How to supply the password

To keep passwords out of shell history and config files, the command line rejects --password and --token, and the config file only accepts references:

Form	Meaning
env:NAME	Read from an environment variable, such as env:BOTMUX_FEEDBACK_PG_PASSWORD
file:<id>	Read a protected secret file in the botmux data directory. Created automatically when you enter a password in the Dashboard; you rarely write it by hand

With env:, the variable must exist both in the terminal where you run botmux feedback storage and in the environment of the botmux service itself, or the service cannot read the password after the switch. The simpler route is to type the password into the Dashboard panel: it is saved as a file readable only by the local user, the config keeps just a reference, and the page never shows it again.

Switch from the Dashboard

Open the Dashboard "Feedback analytics" page and expand "Feedback storage". Only host admins can see this panel.

The screenshot is from an earlier version. The current panel also has an "Authentication" dropdown next to "Backend".

Set "Backend" to PostgreSQL and "Authentication" to "Username / password", then fill in the connection details. Leaving the password blank keeps the previously saved one.

Click "Save candidate settings", then "Test saved connection". The panel shows "Active: sqlite; Candidate: postgresql".

Tick "Confirm maintenance", then:
with history: click "Migrate and enable PostgreSQL";

with no data: click "Empty database: enable directly".


The migration runs in the background. The panel refreshes every few seconds and shows <migration ID>: <phase> <reasons> at the bottom. Settings are locked while it runs.

When it is blocked, a "Resume original migration" button appears (the confirmation box must be ticked). It does the same as resume.

To cancel, expand "Manual recovery and resolution" below, fill in "Reason" and "External verification evidence", keep the confirmation box above ticked, and click "Cancel migration and restore source". The button only appears while a migration is unfinished.

Delivery recovery items

Before migrating, botmux must be sure nothing was "sent with an unknown result", or the data might not line up. There are two kinds:

Kind	What it is
webhook	A delivery of a feedback webhook (feedbackWebhooks in the bot config) that went out without a clear result
send	A botmux send run whose process exited midway, so it is unknown whether the message went out

List them:

botmux feedback storage recovery list

First check on the other side whether it actually arrived (for example the webhook receiver's logs, or whether the message is in the Feishu chat), then record your conclusion:

botmux feedback storage recovery acknowledge \
  --kind webhook --id <id> --fingerprint <fingerprint> --yes \
  --reason "Receiver logs show the event" --evidence "ticket:1234"

Copy --id and --fingerprint from the recovery list output. If the item changed in the meantime you get feedback_recovery_stale; just list again.

Items still in progress (live: true) cannot be acknowledged. Wait for them to end.

Acknowledging only records your decision. It does not resend and does not end the maintenance window. Run resume afterwards.

On the Dashboard, the "List unknown deliveries and send leases" button in "Manual recovery and resolution" does the same thing, with an "Acknowledge verified outcome" button under each item (it also needs the confirmation box ticked and a reason and evidence filled in).

Scripted installs

For automated deployments, set the environment variable BOTMUX_FEEDBACK_CONFIG_FILE to the config file from Step 1. botmux start then saves that config and enables it directly as an empty database (same as enable-empty), without asking. If the config matches the active one, nothing happens.

This is only for fresh installs: if SQLite already has data, it fails with feedback_storage_migration_required. Migrate instead.

FAQ

Can I go from PostgreSQL back to SQLite, or to another PostgreSQL?
Not yet. Migration only supports SQLite → PostgreSQL.

How long is the downtime?
It depends on the data size: running turns must finish, then the data is imported and verified table by table. With modest data it is usually quick. Do it off-peak.

Is the old SQLite file still there afterwards?
Yes. botmux-feedback.sqlite stays in the data directory, retired and no longer written.

Getting feedback_storage_generation_conflict?
The config was changed elsewhere while you were working (for example in an open Dashboard). Run status again and retry. You also get it if you run enable-empty without saving a candidate with configure first.

Related pages: Bot config (bots.json) covers the final-answer feedback card; Dashboard introduces the "Feedback analytics" page; other commands are in CLI commands.

title: Global Settings (config.json)
content:
Some switches apply to the whole machine, not to one bot: when to auto-update, whether to clean up idle sessions on a schedule, who gets pinged when the host is overloaded. They live on the Dashboard's "Global Settings" page. Saving writes them to ~/.botmux/config.json, shared by every bot on this machine.

To change a single bot (working directory, admins, CLI, and so on), see bots.json. For environment variables used inside sessions, see Environment Variables.

Where to change them

Open the Dashboard and click "Global Settings" in the left nav.

The page has its own table of contents with three modules: General, Meeting Agent, and System & Maintenance. Click an entry to jump to it.

Toggles save as soon as you flip them; text inputs (group prefix, proxy, callback URL, and so on) need their "Save" button. Most settings need no restart.

You can also edit ~/.botmux/config.json directly. Every item below lists its JSON field name for hand edits or backups. If "Allow tokenless read-only dashboard access" is on, visitors without a token can view but not change anything.

Quick reference

I want to…	Dashboard location	Field	Default
Install new versions daily	System & Maintenance → Auto Maintenance → Auto update	maintenance.autoUpdate	Off
Restart after a new version is installed	System & Maintenance → Auto Maintenance → Auto restart	maintenance.autoRestart	Off
Close long-unused sessions on a schedule	General → Scheduled tasks → Auto-clean idle sessions on a schedule	sessionCleanup	Off
Get a DM when the host is overloaded	General → Host overload alert	hostOverloadAlert	Off
Run scheduled tasks in a specific timezone	General → Scheduled tasks → Timezone	scheduleTimeZone	Follow host
Prefix group names created by /g	General → Group Creation	groupNamePrefix	None
Hide worktrees in the repo picker	General → Repo Picker	repoPickerMode	Repos + worktrees
Put new worktrees on a larger disk	General → Worktrees	worktreeRoot	Next to the main repo
Download new versions through a proxy	System & Maintenance → Auto Maintenance → GitHub download proxy	httpProxy	Not set
Skip pasting the callback URL after /login	General → Access → OAuth callback base URL	oauthRedirectBase	Not set

Auto update and auto restart

Want botmux to upgrade itself every day → turn on "System & Maintenance → Auto Maintenance → Auto update" and pick a time.

Auto update (off by default): once a day at the chosen time (default 04:00, Beijing time) it checks for a new version and, if there is one, updates using the way you installed botmux (npm / pnpm / Bun global install). It installs only, no restart; the new version takes effect on the next restart.

Auto restart (off by default, requires auto update): restarts only when this run actually installed a newer version. No new version, no restart. It has no schedule of its own.

If any session is busy at that time, the whole run is skipped and moves to the next day, so working sessions are never interrupted.

Auto update is unavailable when running from source (local dev install); the page says so.

After an intentional restart (manual restart, restart after auto update, rollback), the first bot DMs its first administrator a restart report by default. To turn that off, put "maintenance": { "notifyOnRestart": false } in config.json (there is no toggle on the page for it).

{
  "maintenance": {
    "autoUpdate": { "enabled": true, "time": "04:00" },
    "autoRestart": { "enabled": true }
  }
}

Auto-upgrading Codex inside sessions

Location: General → Experimental → Automatically upgrade session Codex versions. Experimental, off by default.

When on and a newer Codex is installed on the machine, running Codex sessions switch to the new process when it is safe and idle, then resume the same thread without starting an extra turn. Sessions with background work, or whose state can't be confirmed safe, wait. The toggle takes effect immediately.

Scheduled cleanup of idle sessions

Lots of open sessions eat memory. Want sessions nobody has used for a while to close on their own → turn on "General → Scheduled tasks → Auto-clean idle sessions on a schedule".

Option	Meaning	Default
Auto-clean idle sessions on a schedule (enabled)	Master switch	Off
Idle threshold (olderThanHours)	How old the last message must be: 24 hours / 72 hours / 7 days	7 days (168)
Check interval (intervalMinutes)	Minutes between checks, minimum 5	60
Archive Codex threads on close / cleanup (archiveCodex)	Archive the matching Codex thread when a session closes (manual close or idle cleanup), restore it on reopen	Off

Override this switch for one Bot under Dashboard “Bot Config → Sessions → Codex native archive” (follow global, on or off; shown for Codex bots only), or with /config set archiveCodex on or /config set archiveCodex off; /config unset archiveCodex restores inheritance. The corresponding Bot entry in bots.json also accepts "archiveCodex": true or false. Command changes apply to subsequent closes and cleanup immediately; an in-progress close keeps its initial value. Previously archived sessions can still be restored.

It uses the same rules as the manual "Clean idle" button on the Session Control page, just unattended. Only truly idle sessions are closed: sessions that are running, locked, waiting on a repo pick, or carrying an alert for you are left alone.

{
  "sessionCleanup": { "enabled": true, "olderThanHours": 72, "intervalMinutes": 60 }
}

Host overload alert

When the host is overloaded, new sessions tend to time out during cold start. Want to know right away → turn on "General → Host overload alert".

Turn on "Enable overload alert".

Pick a notification Bot (one per machine is enough). The page shows the recipient: that Bot's first administrator.

Adjust the two thresholds if needed.

That Bot then checks host load and memory every 30 seconds. It DMs the admin once when the host enters overload and once when it recovers. Bouncing in and out won't spam you (two "entered" alerts are at least 15 minutes apart).

Threshold	Counts as overloaded when	Default
Load enter threshold (enterLoadRatio)	15-minute load average > CPU cores × this value	1.5
Memory enter threshold (enterMemUsedFrac, entered as a percentage)	Used memory reaches this share	92%

The recovery lines are built in (load = cores × 1.0, memory 85%). If you set an enter line at or below its recovery line, the recovery line is pushed down to 95% of the enter line to avoid flapping.

Notes:

The notification Bot must be able to send Feishu messages (not an API-only bot) and must have an administrator.

Environment variables can tune it too: BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ENTER_LOAD_RATIO, BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_EXIT_LOAD_RATIO, BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ENTER_MEM_FRAC, BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_EXIT_MEM_FRAC, BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_MIN_REALERT_MS. They take priority over the page.

BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ALERT=0 turns the feature off completely, whatever the page says.

Memory protection (check before starting a session)

This is on by default and usually needs no attention. Before starting or resuming a session process, botmux checks memory. If:

available memory is below the reserve (default 25% of total memory, capped at 4 GiB), or

memory pressure (Linux PSI full avg10) reaches the limit (default 20%),

it doesn't start the process and replies in the session asking you to free memory and resend. When the shortfall is small, it first suspends a few idle sessions to free memory and tries once more.

There are no toggles for this on the page. Use the CLI to view and change it:

botmux worker-budget status                          # current memory, thresholds, and where they come from
botmux worker-budget set --min-available-mib 2048    # reserve 2 GiB
botmux worker-budget set --max-memory-full-avg10 30  # pressure limit 30%
botmux worker-budget set --memory-admission-enabled false   # turn the check off
botmux worker-budget set --session-memory-max-mib 4096      # cap each session at 4 GiB (needs cgroup v2)
botmux worker-budget unset                           # drop overrides, back to defaults

These map to the worker field in config.json (memoryAdmissionEnabled, minAvailableMemoryBytes, maxMemoryFullAvg10, sessionMemoryMaxBytes). They don't change how many sessions each bot keeps resident (that's maxLiveWorkers in bots.json).

Scheduled task timezone

Location: General → Scheduled tasks → Timezone. Default: follow host.

Scheduled tasks fire, parse phrases like "tomorrow 9:00", and display times on cards and the Dashboard in this timezone. If the server is abroad but you're in Beijing, pick Asia/Shanghai.

Priority (earlier wins):

Environment variable BOTMUX_SCHEDULE_TIMEZONE

Timezone chosen on the page (scheduleTimeZone)

Host system timezone

An invalid timezone name is skipped and the next level is used. The auto-update time is not affected; it always uses Beijing time.

Group creation and repo picker

/g group name prefix (General → Group Creation, groupNamePrefix): groups created with /group or /g get this text in front of their name, e.g. AI-chat·. Other ways of creating groups don't. Clear it and save to turn it off; takes effect within about 2 seconds. See Create a session group.

Repo picker card mode (General → Repo Picker, repoPickerMode): all (default, repos plus their worktrees) or repos (main repos only). With repos, /repo <worktree path> still takes you into a worktree.

Worktree directory (General → Worktrees, worktreeRoot): botmux creates new worktrees under this directory, e.g. /data00/worktrees. Useful when the system disk is small and a larger data disk is mounted. Worktrees are laid out under it by the main repo's own path: a worktree of /root/iserver/botmux becomes /data00/worktrees/root/iserver/botmux-wt-…, so repos with the same name in different places don't collide. Use an absolute path (may start with ~/) to an existing, writable directory. Only affects worktrees created from then on; existing ones stay where they are and keep working, also if you change the directory again later. If the directory later goes missing or stops being writable (e.g. the data disk isn't mounted, or was remounted read-only), new worktrees are created next to the main repo instead and a warning is logged. Clear it and save to go back to creating them next to the main repo; takes effect within about 2 seconds.

Network and access

Setting	Location	Purpose
GitHub download proxy (httpProxy)	System & Maintenance → Auto Maintenance	HTTP proxy for GitHub downloads when the standalone binary updates itself, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890. If empty, HTTPS_PROXY / HTTP_PROXY are used, otherwise it connects directly. npm / pnpm / Bun installs use their own proxy settings
OAuth callback base URL (oauthRedirectBase)	General → Access	After a Feishu authorization (e.g. /login), Feishu redirects here and the Dashboard finishes it, so you don't paste the callback URL by hand. Useful when botmux doesn't run on your own computer. Enter scheme + host + port only, e.g. http://10.1.2.3:7891. After changing it, open any bot's "Session-group tag" row and click "Fix Open Platform callback", otherwise Feishu returns error 20029
Remote terminal access (remoteAccess)	General → Access	Off by default. Shown only when this machine is bound to the central platform. When on, session terminals, card terminal buttons, and webhook URLs use platform links; off uses local links

For the web terminal itself, see Web Terminal.

How built-in skills reach the CLI

botmux's built-in skills (sending messages, creating schedules, and so on) need to be handed to the CLI. For CLIs that only have a global skills directory, such as Codex and OpenCode, there are three modes (skills.builtinInjection):

Value	What it does
prompt (default)	Leaves the CLI's global directory alone; puts a short catalog in the session prompt and fetches full instructions on demand. Doesn't affect CLIs you run by hand
global	Installs into the CLI's global skills directory for the most native experience, but your own manual codex runs will see them too
off	Adds neither; only a pointer to botmux --help

This is the machine-wide default. Change it with botmux skills injection [global|prompt|off|unset]; no argument shows the current value. If a bot sets skillInjection in bots.json, the bot's own value wins. See Skill.

Separate sessions for each person in a group (XPI, experimental) {#xpi}

Off by default. While it's off, everyone in a group shares one session: a message someone sends while the bot is busy is queued as usual and handled after the current task.

When on, each human in the same group gets their own CLI context and git worktree, so people can work in parallel without interrupting each other:

Messages are still public in the group; each person's just go to their own "lane".

Quoting a task someone else is running goes through a suggestion / confirmation flow instead of jumping into their task; other messages continue in the sender's own lane.

Send /lane status in a topic to see your lane's branch, worktree, uncommitted changes and unpushed commits; /lane close closes your lane safely (it refuses while a task is running or files are uncommitted, pushes unpublished commits before reclaiming, and never merges or deletes branches on its own).

When an agent messages another bot, it has to say whether that's a separate task or input for the current one with botmux send --as independent|suggestion.

To turn it on: Dashboard Global Settings → General → Experimental → Cross-principal interruption isolation (XPI), which is dashboard.crossPrincipalInterruption: true in config.json. It applies to every bot on this machine and takes effect from the next message, no restart needed. To force it on or off for a single daemon process, set BOTMUX_XPI_ENABLED=true / false in its environment; that wins over the Dashboard switch.

Keep it off when people need to share one context and set of files; turn it on when their tasks are fully independent.

FAQ

Do I need to restart after editing config.json?
Most toggles on the page take effect as soon as you save. After hand-editing the file, check the values on the page; when in doubt, run botmux restart.

Auto update is on, so why didn't it update?
Possible reasons: a session was busy at that time (moved to the next day); botmux wasn't running at that time and came back more than an hour later (skipped for that day); you're already on the latest version; this is a local dev install or an unsupported install layout (shown next to the "Auto Maintenance" title).

I never get overload alerts?
Check that a notification Bot is selected, that Bot is online, and it has an administrator. Also check whether BOTMUX_OVERLOAD_ALERT=0 is set.

Should backups include config.json?
Yes. When moving machines, take bots.json, .env, config.json, and data/ together. See Environment Variables.
